content_metadata.description: This video tutorial explains various separation techniques for liquid-solid heterogeneous mixtures using animated illustrations and clear voiceover narration.

qAndA.question: In the sedimentation and decantation process, what is the settled sand at the bottom of the beaker called?

qAndA.answer: Centrifugation is helpful for separating mixtures that contain very fine solid particles suspended in a liquid.
qAndA.question: What kind of mixtures is centrifugation particularly useful for separating?

qAndA.answer: The porous plate supports the filter paper and allows the liquid to pass through while retaining the solid particles.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the porous plate in the Buchner funnel during vacuum filtration?

qAndA.answer: The water pump extracts air from the Buchner flask, creating a lower pressure inside the flask, which accelerates filtration.
qAndA.question: How does a water pump contribute to vacuum filtration?
What is the liquid collected in the Buchner flask after vacuum filtration called?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Separation techniques of heterogeneous mixtures
Case of liquid solid mixtures
Sedimentation and decantation
Separating a mixture of mud and water
Allow the muddy water to stand for a while
The sand particles settle at the bottom of the beaker
This is called sedimentation
Sedimentation allows for the appearance of two distinct phases
The liquid phase and the solid phase or sediment
The solid phase is called the sediment
To separate both phases, the liquid is slowly poured into another beaker
This is called decantation
Both phases were separated by decantation
The mixture was separated by sedimentation followed by decantation
Centrifugation
In some cases, sedimentation may take a long time
This is the case of very fine solid particles suspended in a liquid
Centrifugation can be used to accelerate the sedimentation of the solid phase
For example, centrifugation can be used to separate water from extremely fine particles of sand
that are suspended in water
Separating a mixture of water and extremely fine particles of sand
The mixture is poured in several centrifuge test tubes
The test tubes are ready to be put in the centrifuge
The tubes containing the mixtures are now introduced in the centrifuge
The centrifuge rotates the tube at a very high speed
which forces the fine solid particles to settle at the bottom of the tubes
The tubes are now removed from the centrifuge
The fine solid particles are deposited at the bottom of the tubes
Sedimentation allows for the appearance of two clear phases
The liquid phase and the solid phase are sediment
The liquid is ready to be decanted
Decantation
The liquid phase and the solid phase are separated by decantation
Filtration
Separating orange juice from its pulp
The mixture is poured in another beaker through a filter paper
The solid pulp is ready to be put in the centrifuge
The mixture is poured in another beaker through a filter paper
The solid pulp is retained by the filter paper
while the liquid juice passes through it to the other beaker
The solid phase and the liquid phase were separated by filtration
Vacuum filtration
Filtration may be accelerated by creating a difference in pressure on both sides of the filtration funnel
Buckner funnel
This is done by connecting the flask to running water
Equipment of vacuum filtration
Stand
Buckner funnel
Porous plate
Rubber bung
Buckner flask
Water pump
Rubber tubing
Tap
Place a moistened filter paper in the buckner funnel
Open the tap
Running water extracts air from the buckner flask
This lowers the pressure inside the flask
The difference in pressure between both sides of the flask
will accelerate the movement of the liquid downwards towards the flask
Pressure outside the flask is bigger than the pressure inside the flask
Gently pour the mixture in the funnel
End of vacuum filtration
The solid particles are retained on the filter paper
The liquid phase is recovered in the flask, close the tap
Residue
Filtrate
Scrape the residue with a spatula into another container
End of separation techniques of heterogeneous liquid solid mixtures
